en: Now, Bun's WebSocket feature does also have
a client version. It's not in the browser,
there we use the browser API, but you could
build a CLI WebSocket client, for example,
or some other client that's powered by Bun.
So here in the CLI client.ts file, I have a
very simple CLI where I get some
input from the user for the username and the
room, or I assume some defaults if no
arguments were passed to the CLI command.
And then just as in the browser, we
establish a connection by preparing a URL
and using that same WebSocket API we used in
the browser.
But this file will not be executed by the
browser. It will be executed by Bun because
in my package.json file, it's this CLI
script that would execute that file using
Bun as you see.
But Bun, just like the browser, also
supports this WebSocket API, the standard
web WebSocket API.
Just as Bun supports the standard response
or request APIs, for example.
And therefore we can use WebSockets here
just as we did in the browser, listen to the
same kind of events, use the same API
because it is the same API
but now powered by Bun.
So with the Bun server still up and running,
I could run bun run CLI
and maybe connect as Max to chat.
So now Max joined chat
and I could say, hi there,
and see my message here and then open
another CLI session.
So run bun run CLI
Andy and same topic, same room chat.
Hi, this is
Andy. And if I do that, you'll see in the
Max chat,
I see, hi, this is Andy.
And if I write
hi there, of course, as Max,
that also shows up here. So same logic, but
now this is a Bun client. This is not a web
client. If I close my session here with
Andy, I also see that message here.
And therefore you can use Bun not just for
setting up a server, but also for setting up
a client if you want to.
